newsitem.title: USA: Chevron completes Florida drilling plans.
newsitem.headline: Chevron completes Florida drilling plans.

text.p: Chevron USA Inc has completed a controversial application to drill for natural gas in federal waters about 25 miles off the northwest coast of Florida, the U.S. Minerals Management Service said on Monday.
The plans, which are expected to spark protests from Florida environmental groups, must be approved by federal and state regulators in a process that could take up to two years, the agency said.

Chevron expects to drill 12-21 wells and produce 300-450 million cubic feet of natural gas per day from the prolific Destin Dome formation with a March 1999 start-up date, said the MMS, an Interior Department agency which regulates oil and gas production in federal waters of Gulf of Mexico.
The plans, if approved, would end a long-time moratorium on drilling off the coast of Florida.
A Chevron spokesman was not immediately available for comment.

"It will take about a year to prepare a draft EIS (environmental impact statement) to examine the potential effects of the project on the marine, coastal and human environments," the MMS said in a statement.
Anticipating a firestorm of protests from environmentalists and the state's tourism industry, the agency last year opened a regional office in Pensacola.

Chevron has drilled several exploration wells into the Destin Dome formation about 25 miles south of Pensacola. The dome lies on the eastern edge of the Norphlet Trend, a geologic formation believed to be the largest natural gas play in the continental United States.
Chevron drilled two discovery wells in the area in 1987, three years after it began accumulating lease rights to 11 blocks off the Florida coast for $13.1 million.
The company has since drilled two more discovery wells, the latest in November 1995. That well flowed at 41 million cubic feet per day, the MMS said.
Chevron is partners with Murphy Oil Corp's Murphy Exploration and Production Co and DuPont's Conoco in the project.
